target_stage: Supreme Court civil appeal by special leave from the Delhi High Court's second-appeal judgment

IK-114533:L148:span1.text: the respondent applied under cite16†section 14 of the above Act to the Rent Controller, Delhi for evicting the appellant on the ground that she had sub-let the entire premises to one Sohan Singh who, according to the respondent, was running a business under the name of Royal Dispensing Chemists and Druggists in the shop.

IK-114533:L149:span2.text: It was further alleged that the appellant was charging a fabulous amount as rent from her sub-tenant Sohan Singh.

IK-114533:L149:span3.text: The appellant in her written statement admitted the tenancy

IK-114533:L149:span5.text: She alleged that Sohan Singh was her husband

IK-114533:L149:span6.text: from the time of the lease the business of a Chemist was being run there in the premises by her husband and she also occasionally helped him in the running of the business.

IK-114533:L150:span7.text: Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife and, therefore, there was no question of any sub--letting by the appellant of the premises.

IK-114533:L150:span8.text: That finding was confirmed in appeal by the Rent Control Tribunal, Delhi.

IK-114533:L169:span9.text: The respondent himself in his testimony admitted that he had never himself made any enquiry as to whether Sohan Singh and the appellant are husband and wife or not.

IK-114533:L170:span10.text: Neither any talks regarding sub-letting took place in my presence, nor the rent was paid in my presence,

IK-114533:L171:span11.text: he was shown a typed copy of it and this he accepted as a true copy.

IK-114533:L171:span12.text: The true copy disclosed that the appellant was accepted as the wife of Sohan Singh.
